fields.description:
Author ADR 0106 defining **remote-anchored below-horizon HISTORY reclamation** whose PRIMARY lever
is **commit/tree collapse** (retired-event GC is a secondary companion, not the pack lever), and
promote docs/concurrency.md §I1 'permanent retention' (epic b306) from a follow-up note to an
implemented+cross-referenced model. This ADR is the causal-stability contract that unblocks S1-S3.
(ADR number is 0106 — 0105 was taken by an unrelated ADR that landed on origin/main.)

Scope (docs-only): the horizon config key (default 30d, portable, no CI-provider dependency); the
remote-reachability computation (a collapse checkpoint commit reachable from the sync remote's
tickets ref for >= N days); the stale-clone detection + FORCED remote-override protocol on reconnect
(a clone whose last convergence is older than N days overrides local with remote rather than
reintroducing pre-collapse history by rebase); the **C1-C5 causal-stability boundary at the
commit/tree-rewrite level**; SNAPSHOT authorship_ledger carriage OR enforce_since re-anchor for
signature/authorship verifiability; the portable rewrite primitive and per-backend publish-swap;
and a proof that invariants I1-I9 still hold. State the accepted residual: a >N-day-drifted clone's
divergent local work is discarded. (Re-scoped 2026-08-29 from '.retired-only' to the
commit/tree-collapse lever - see epic comment 'Child-roster re-scope'.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md` exists with the ADR shape (`# ADR 0106:`
  title, `- **Status:**`, `## Context`, `## Decision`, `## Consequences`).
- [ ] The ADR defines the N-day horizon as a portable config key (default 30d) with NO single-CI-provider
  trigger (the `project.portability` criterion applies).
- [ ] The ADR specifies remote-reachability (collapse checkpoint reachable from the sync remote tickets
  ref for >= N days) and the stale-clone FORCED remote-override protocol on reconnect.
- [ ] The ADR states the C1-C5 causal-stability boundary at the commit/tree-rewrite level and how
  signature/authorship verifiability is preserved (SNAPSHOT authorship_ledger carriage OR enforce_since
  re-anchor).
- [ ] The ADR names the history-rewrite primitive as core-git (`git fast-import` / `mktree`+`commit-tree`,
  NO third-party `git filter-repo`) and, per backend, the publish-swap: git-ref `--force-with-lease` CAS
  for git remotes, and an exclusive push-locked bundle-set replacement bypassing the `git-remote-s3`
  auto-doctor for the S3 backend — citing the auto-doctor never-discard-a-head resurrection hazard
  (ADR 0093 / `src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py`) and proving its bypass safe under C1-C5.
- [ ] The ADR proves invariants I1-I9 hold under reclamation and names the accepted residual
  (>N-day-drifted clone divergent local work discarded).
- [ ] `docs/concurrency.md` §I1 is promoted from 'follow-up' to implemented and cross-references ADR 0106.

## Verification
- `test -f docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md` and
  `grep -n '^# ADR 0106:' docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md` and
  `grep -n '^## \(Context\|Decision\|Consequences\)' docs/adr/0106-remote-anchored-history-reclamation.md`
  confirm the ADR shape and title.
- `grep -n '0106' docs/concurrency.md` confirms the I1 cross-reference landed.
- `make lint` passes (docs change introduces no lint regressions); `rebar review-plan unlikely-zealous-skua`
  re-run confirms the plan is admissible.
